title: Is ‘ferritin face’ a real thing?
description:
You might’ve seen lots of chat online about ‘ferritin face’ alongside zoomed in before and after pics of people’s faces. Some claim that changes in their appearance, like pale skin and hair loss, are down to having low ferritin levels.

But what even is ferritin? It’s the protein responsible for storing iron in the body. Iron is important for creating red blood cells, which carry oxygen around the body. It’s needed for things like your energy levels, skin and hair health. So, can you tell if your ferritin levels are low just by your face? We break it down with the BBC’s Zara Salaria and Dr Aziza Sesay, who specialises in female health.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討社群媒體上熱門的「鐵蛋白臉」 (ferritin face) 流行趨勢，以及低鐵蛋白對人體健康的影響。鐵蛋白是負責儲存鐵質的蛋白質，雖然缺鐵可能導致疲倦、掉髮與眼袋等狀況，但「鐵蛋白臉」並非正式的醫學診斷，且深色膚色者的外在徵候可能較不明顯。專家提醒，血液檢查是確認鐵蛋白濃度的唯一方法，民眾應避免僅憑 TikTok 等網路資訊自行診斷或過量補充鐵劑。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores the social media trend known as 'ferritin face,' where users link symptoms like dark eye circles, pale skin, and hair loss to low ferritin levels. Presenter Hannah Gelbart, BBC reporter Zara Salaria, and Dr. Aziza Sesay explain that ferritin is the protein that stores iron, and 'ferritin face' is not an official medical diagnosis. They highlight that visual signs vary across skin tones and stress that a blood test is the only accurate way to determine ferritin levels before treating any deficiency.
